scenes.0: Same robot. Same task. One run succeeds, one fails. Move the start three centimeters, and it fails every time. Our review found that weakness. We fixed it with fifty new demonstrations, and re-tested it on a sealed schedule: twelve for twelve, where the old policy went three for twelve. But at the trained spot, the evidence is still not enough. So QuantGate does not approve it yet.
scenes.1: For quantization, [[pause:0.4]] we need to pick the candidate that has earned its next test, not an approval. [[pause:0.5]] That's why robot researchers need Quant Gate.
scenes.2: This is an S O one oh one arm running an A C T policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, on a [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/) [Orin](/ˈɔɹɪn/) Nano Super. We taught it with one hundred and twenty teleoperated demonstrations, and trained it with [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) Jobs. From that one policy, we built twenty-six candidate engines with TensorRT: full precision, half precision, and twenty-four [int](/ˈɪnt/) eight builds that differ only in how they were calibrated. Every trial runs from a sealed, interleaved schedule. The operator sees only trial numbers, and the results stay sealed until all the trials are logged.
scenes.3: First, measure on the real device. On this [Jetson](/dʒˈɛtsən/), half precision was the fastest engine, and the cheapest per inference, not [int](/ˈɪnt/) eight. On the arm, every candidate succeeded ninety to a hundred percent of the time. And the offline audit's top picks did no better than random picks. Twenty-five trials cannot tell them apart.
scenes.4: What moved success was the deployment condition, not the precision. A new can worked forty-eight out of forty-eight. Without the gripper pads, success fell to eight out of twenty-four. So the fix was data: fifty demonstrations at shifted positions, fine-tuned in twenty-five minutes on [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) Jobs.
scenes.5: The A I layers get checked too. In its first setup, Cosmos Reason, on a [Nebius](/nˈɛbiəs/) A I Endpoint, caught one failure in twenty-one. We tested it like any other component, on held-out recordings, and a validated question caught twenty of twenty-one. [Nemotron](/nˈimOtɹˌɑn/) Super on Token Factory explains the review in words, while every verdict and number comes from code.
scenes.6: So QuantGate answers three questions. Which candidate do I validate first? Half precision. Which do I distrust? Broken calibrations, which a simple input check catches, and any engine whose files no longer match what was audited. Can I approve deployment? Not yet. The review lists exactly which trials, and which rule changes, are still missing.
scenes.7: Quant Gate. Earn the next test, not the approval.
